## Quick answer

Ethanol pays off when its price is below 70% of the gasoline price. That is a
general rule: the real break-even point depends on how your own car burns each
fuel.

## Why the rule works

A flex-fuel engine usually travels about 70% as far on one liter of ethanol as
on one liter of gasoline. The 70% rule is the point where the cost per
kilometer is the same.

## Measure your own car

Fill the tank, note the odometer, drive normally and fill it again. Divide the
distance by the liters used to get kilometers per liter for each fuel, then
compare the two numbers.
